question: What is the primary purpose of a nursing audit?

options.A: Punishing staff members who make documentation errors
options.C: Calculating monthly hospital revenue from patient bills
options.D: Evaluating nursing care against established standards

explanation: Nursing audits focus strictly on assessing clinical care and documentation against pre-determined professional benchmarks to ensure quality. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is a nursing audit considered an essential part of clinical governance?

options.A: It replaces the need for daily nursing shift handovers
options.B: It enforces strict professional accountability and quality care
options.C: It guarantees that hospitals receive government funding
options.D: It eliminates all potential risks of clinical negligence

explanation: Clinical governance relies on systematic evaluation tools like audits to maintain high standards of patient safety and professional responsibility. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which objective is a primary focus of nursing audits within quality assurance?

options.A: Minimizing the purchasing of hospital consumables
options.B: Reducing the overall duration of nursing education
options.C: Increasing the daily number of patient admissions
options.D: Promoting uniform and standardized nursing procedures

explanation: Standardizing care ensures that every patient receives consistent, evidence-based interventions regardless of which shift or ward they are in. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: What happens when healthcare facilities fail to conduct regular nursing audits?

options.A: Clinical standards gradually drift and patient care becomes inconsistent
options.B: Nursing staff automatically improve their documentation accuracy
options.C: Hospital management saves a significant amount of administrative time
options.D: Patients experience shorter recovery times in the ward

explanation: Without regular monitoring and feedback loops, adherence to clinical protocols naturally declines over time. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: When is a retrospective nursing audit conducted?

options.A: During the emergency triage assessment phase
options.B: After the patient has been discharged from the hospital
options.C: While the patient is actively receiving care in the ward
options.D: Before the patient is admitted to the clinical unit

explanation: Retrospective audits analyze completed health records after the patient has left the facility. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: A nurse manager wants to observe ongoing care and immediately correct documentation gaps while the patient is still admitted. Which audit type should be used?
explanation: Concurrent audits take place in real-time during the patient's hospital stay, enabling immediate feedback and correction of care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the very first step in conducting a nursing audit?

options.A: Purchasing new computers for the medical records department
options.B: Selecting a specific clinical topic or problem to evaluate
options.C: Discharging all patients currently in the surgical ward
options.D: Punishing staff members for poor documentation habits

explanation: Every audit must begin by defining a clear focus or clinical area that requires evaluation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is establishing explicit audit criteria essential before collecting data?

options.A: It provides a clear, objective benchmark to measure actual practice against
options.B: It eliminates the need for any statistical data analysis later
options.C: It guarantees that every nurse will receive a positive performance review
options.D: It allows auditors to change the rules depending on who is on duty

explanation: Explicit criteria ensure that the evaluation is consistent, fair, and based on predetermined professional standards rather than subjective opinion. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: What legal and clinical maxim guides nursing documentation reviews during an audit?

options.B: Patient memory replaces missing nursing notes
options.C: If it is not documented, it was not done
options.D: Documentation is optional for experienced nurses

explanation: In both legal and professional contexts, unrecorded nursing actions cannot be legally verified as having taken place. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which source of information forms the core of most nursing audits?

options.A: Patient clinical records and documentation charts
options.B: Personal diary entries written by patients

explanation: Patient records provide the documented evidence of assessments, interventions, and evaluations performed by nursing staff. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary danger of looking only at raw compliance percentages without investigating root causes?

options.A: Management might blame individuals for systemic or institutional failures
options.B: Patients will experience immediate improvements in recovery rates
options.C: The hospital will immediately lose its official accreditation status
options.D: Nurses will stop charting vital signs completely across all wards

explanation: Blaming individuals without examining underlying operational or environmental barriers often fails to fix the actual problem. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: What statistical measure is commonly used to present nursing audit compliance data?
explanation: Percentages and proportions provide a clear, easy-to-understand metric showing how often standards were successfully met. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: What action is necessary to officially 'close the quality loop' after an audit?

options.A: Shredding all previous patient records to protect privacy
options.B: Conducting a follow-up re-audit to measure the impact of changes
options.C: Stopping all future clinical evaluations in the hospital
options.D: Transferring all nursing staff to different hospital departments

explanation: A complete audit cycle requires re-evaluating practice after interventions are introduced to verify that genuine improvement occurred. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is sharing audit results directly with frontline nursing staff important?

options.A: It fosters a transparent culture and encourages collaborative problem-solving
options.B: It ensures that nurses are financially penalized for documentation errors
options.C: It prevents patients from reading their own medical charts
options.D: It gives nurses administrative authority over hospital budgets

explanation: Involving frontline staff in reviewing results helps them take ownership of solutions and improves overall engagement in quality care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to nursing audits in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Severe staff shortages and high patient-to-nurse ratios
options.B: Excessive availability of fully automated electronic health records
options.C: Inconsistent administrative support and funding constraints
options.D: Heavy reliance on paper-based record systems prone to loss

explanation: The question uses a negative frame. Most Nigerian public hospitals still struggle with paper records rather than having excessive electronic systems, making that option incorrect as a barrier. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)

question: How do heavy patient-to-nurse ratios directly impact the nursing audit process?

options.A: Overworked nurses have less time for thorough documentation and audit activities
options.B: Patients prefer to audit their own medical charts during admission
options.C: Hospitals have extra financial resources to hire specialized audit teams
options.D: Nurses automatically complete their documentation faster and more accurately

explanation: High workloads force nurses to prioritize direct bedside care over paperwork, frequently resulting in incomplete records and little time for audit participation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)
